title: Place the RawNode-construction proof for accepted configs: §7.10 assigns it to W08, which cannot depend on vendored raft
description:
## Context
PLAN.md §7.10 (config validation, the raft-rs Config::validate bullet) says that a config the parser accepts can never fail at RawNode construction, "proven by a W08 test that constructs a node from every accepted fixture config". W08 cannot host that test:
- W08's area is types and config (§12.2); its only dependency is W04.
- types is a pure domain crate. DEP-RULE allows the vendored raft only in engine crates, and dev-dependencies count (Appendix A, AGENTS.md Dependencies).
- The vendored raft is not a workspace member yet. raft_adapter is created by W13, which depends on W02 and W11.
- W08's own §12.2 acceptance row does not mention the RawNode test.
Found while starting W08.1 (br-w08-1-config-parser-rules-gwj).

## Requirements
O-5, CD-3. §7.10 (the raft-rs Config::validate rule), §12.2 W08 and W13 rows, Appendix A tiers.

## Options
- **A (recommended).** W08.1 encodes every raft-rs 0.7 Config::validate constraint as a parser rule, each with its own test:
  - node id != 0;
  - heartbeat > 0;
  - election_tick > heartbeat_tick;
  - min >= election_tick, and min < max;
  - max_inflight_msgs > 0;
  - LeaseBased reads need check_quorum (keyval pins Safe reads with check-quorum on);
  - max_uncommitted_size >= max_size_per_msg.

  W08.1 also commits the accepted fixture configs as a corpus (config/fixtures/). W13, which owns the Config -> raft::Config mapping, adds the test that constructs a RawNode from every accepted fixture. Plan change: §7.10 reads "a W13 test", and W13's acceptance gains that line.
- **B.** W08.1 adds the vendored raft to the workspace and creates raft_adapter now, holding only the mapping function and the test. This is outside W08's area, runs ahead of W02 and W13 (§12.3 edges), adds raft's dependency tree to Cargo.lock now, and risks P6 (a crate created early for one test).

## Area
PLAN.md (owner), registry/workgraph.toml (W13 accept, if A).

## Acceptance
Owner decision recorded here. If A: PLAN §7.10 and §12.2 W13 are amended (plan-change), and W08.1 ships its rules and the fixture corpus without the RawNode test.

## Out of scope
Implementing W13.

title: RAFT-AUDIT: static scan keeping W02.2's 'none on any path' verdicts true in vendor/raft
description:
## Context
The W02.2 audit (spike/raft-audit.md) proved by reading tree 4ab81467 that vendored raft-rs has:
- exactly one entropy site (raft.rs:2807-2819, thread_rng);
- no clocks, no threads on production paths, no randomly seeded maps other than quorum.rs AckIndexer (test-only), and no pointer formatting.
A vendor update or the W02.3 patch could silently break these verdicts.

## Requirements
P4, T-3; PLAN §7.3 (the audit's 'unproven items get a test').

## Area
xtask: a new leaf module plus a check.rs catalogue row. These are shared facades, so sequence them in Agent Mail thread xtask-shared-facades.

## Design
A static check over vendor/raft/*/src, excluding #[cfg(test)] modules, *_test.rs and doc comments. It fails on:
- thread_rng or rand:: (expected count 1 before W02.3, 0 after; the expected count lives in VENDOR.toml or the check);
- Instant, SystemTime or thread::spawn;
- std::collections::HashMap or HashSet outside quorum.rs's AckIndexer;
- {:p}.
Each violation names the file and line.

## Acceptance
./dev check RAFT-AUDIT passes on the committed tree with nonzero cases. Fixtures, one per forbidden pattern, make it fail.

## Out of scope
Changing vendored files.

comments.author: charlie
comments.text: Design note (JadeOx). The bead's literal rule, 'std::collections::HashMap or HashSet outside quorum.rs AckIndexer', would fail on the current tree: raft/src/lib.rs:605-607 names std::collections::HashMap/HashSet to define the crate's FxHash aliases, which the W02.2 audit (H-1) judges deterministic per build. RAFT-AUDIT therefore targets the actual hazard, a randomly seeded std collection. It flags RandomState; std HashMap/HashSet named or imported with the default hasher; and any use of a std-bound HashMap/HashSet name, except quorum.rs's import and its 'type AckIndexer' (H-2). A qualified std collection whose last generic argument is DefaultHashBuilder is allowed only while every 'type DefaultHashBuilder' is exactly std::hash::BuildHasherDefault<fxhash::FxHasher>; that pin is checked too. Other rules: entropy (thread_rng, rand:: paths, extern crate rand) is counted per source line against EXPECTED_ENTROPY_SITES = 0 (post-W02.3); Instant and SystemTime; thread::spawn, scope and Builder; and {:p}-style format specs in string literals. Pointer casts are not flagged, because majority.rs:84 has a legitimate 'as *mut _' that formats nothing. Excluded: comments (doc comments included), #[cfg(test)] items (inline only, because lib.rs declares raft both #[cfg(test)] and #[cfg(not(test))]), #![cfg(test)] files and *_test.rs. Acceptance labels: accept:RAFT-AUDIT for the static check on the committed tree; the per-pattern fixtures are unit tests in xtask/src/raft_audit.rs that run in XTASK and the T0 gate.

title: Bound accept trees and per-checkout target dirs (~470 MB each; disk at 6.8 GB free)
description:
## Context
Every checkout path now builds into its own cargo target dir (br-gate-shared-target-dir-dtqu): `$KEYVAL_TARGET_BASE/keyval-checkout-<sha256(realpath)[:16]>`, about 470 MB each. W07.3's `./dev accept` materialises each tree into `.local/accept/<tree-id>/` (PLAN §11.3 step 7, W07 acceptance), so every accepted tree adds a new target dir, a ~1 min cold build. The same holds for each worker's frozen candidate copies. Nothing removes them: §10.10 makes `./dev prune` (W46, M4) the **only** sanctioned deletion of generated `.local/` artifacts, under the Q9 rule (keep the last 5 gate runs, the last 5 accept trees, and every failing run's artifacts).

Measured 2026-10-03: free disk on `/` fell from 9.3 GB to 6.8 GB in one afternoon of M0 work (38 GB disk). At ~470 MB per accept, roughly a dozen more closures exhaust the disk, long before W46 exists.

## Requirements
CD-9 (a limit on everything), Q9 retention, §10.10 prune policy. Coordinate with W46.

## Decision needed (owner)
Pick one:
- (a) Land the Q9 subset of `./dev prune` now. It covers accept trees and their target dirs plus stale per-checkout target dirs whose checkout path no longer exists, and logs every removal in a receipt. W46 then extends it.
- (b) Accept trees share one target dir. That reverses the per-checkout rule for accept, which is safe only because each accept tree is freshly materialised.
- (c) Manual owner cleanup until W46.

## Acceptance (for a)
- `./dev prune` keeps the newest 5 accept trees and every failing run's artifacts.
- It removes older accept trees together with their `keyval-checkout-*` target dirs.
- It logs each removal in a receipt.
- A dry-run mode exists.
- Fixtures cover the retention boundary (N−1/N/N+1).

## Out of scope
T1–T3 run retention (W46).

title: AGENTS.md: say in the Lint Policy that the determinism ban also covers tests in deterministic crates
description:
Context: the M0 audit (2026-10-03, /data/projects/keyval-audit-2 @ f283702) found that the determinism lints (`clippy::disallowed_methods`/`disallowed_types`) also fire inside `#[cfg(test)]` code in deterministic crates (a `std::env::var` call in a test fn was rejected). That is stricter than CD-8's test carve-out for unwrap/expect/panic, and it is not written down anywhere. Owner decision 2026-10-03: keep the ban. Tests in deterministic crates must be deterministic too and use the same ports with seeded fakes; a test that really needs the real environment, clock or filesystem belongs in an adapter or harness crate. title: BUG: AGENTS.md drifts from PLAN section 11.5 (rules 3 and 12, git session boilerplate)
description:
## Conflict (filed per PLAN.md §0.4 — lower source corrected to match higher; PLAN.md wins)

The committed AGENTS.md restatement of the §11.5 agent rules has drifted from PLAN.md v1.6:

1. **Rule 12 contradicts D-72.** AGENTS.md (## Agent Rules, rule 12) says: "When you close a bead that implements a requirement, set it to `active`." PLAN.md §11.5 rule 12 (revised v1.5, decision D-72) says the OPPOSITE: "**Never edit a requirement's status by hand:** activation is derived by `./dev commit --close` when the last listing bead closes (§10.13), and the registry gate rejects hand-edited statuses." An agent following AGENTS.md as written would hand-edit `registry/requirements.toml` and be rejected by the W05 gate — or worse, re-introduce the premature-activation bug D-72 closed.
2. **Rule 3 omits the `conflict` label.** AGENTS.md rule 3 says a genuine checker/model bug gets a bead labelled `needs-owner`; PLAN.md §11.5 rule 3 requires ONE bead with BOTH labels `conflict` AND `needs-owner` (§13 item 10 counts `conflict` beads, so the omission would let a checker-bug bead escape the Definition-of-Done check).
3. **Minor:** the tool-generated "Beads Workflow Integration" section's "Session Protocol" shows raw `git add` / `git commit` / `git push`, contradicting this repo's Git Discipline section (commits only via `./dev commit`; no remote exists). The bv-generated trailer's Git Policy note partially mitigates; the hand-written sections win, but the contradiction inside one file invites mistakes during the bootstrap window where raw commits ARE temporarily in use.

## Resolution
AGENTS.md is below PLAN.md in precedence, so AGENTS.md is corrected to match §11.5 verbatim on rules 3 and 12. The natural vehicle is W01.5 (writes AGENTS.md with all 18 rules; its acceptance requires every §11.5 rule present — W01's gate checks the list). For item 3, add a one-line banner in the Git Discipline section stating it overrides any tool-generated git instructions below. Close this bead when the committed AGENTS.md matches §11.5 exactly.

Both locations cited: AGENTS.md lines "## Agent Rules" items 3 and 12 + "### Session Protocol"; PLAN.md §11.5 rules 3 and 12, §10.13 (status lifecycle), D-72.
acceptance_criteria: Committed AGENTS.md matches section 11.5 verbatim on rules 3 and 12; Git Discipline section states it overrides tool-generated git instructions; verified by W01 gate check of the rule list
notes: Second-round audit readback: the shared checkout already contains the rule-3 dual-label correction, receipt-derived rule-12 activation, and the Git Discipline override banner. Preserve those prior edits. This existing conflict stays open until its required committed-tree acceptance receipt exists; a correct working-copy readback alone does not permit closure.

title: Add JSON Schemas for ./dev --json outputs in schemas/ with validation tests (O-6)
description:
## Context

title: E2E: CLI-vs-real-cluster journey script, registered as a T1 check — discovered work
description:
## Context (discovered work — closes a coverage gap)
The conformance suite exercises the HTTP API, the lifecycle smoke exercises crash recovery, and W33's tests exercise the CLI — but nothing GATED exercises the full user journey of the real CLI against a real five-node cluster (demo m3 does, but demos are owner-facing, not checks). This bead adds that end-to-end script as a registered T1-tier check, following the W01.6 test-logging standard throughout.

## The journey (scripted, non-interactive, every step logged: action, expected, observed, duration; non-zero exit on first failure)
1. Fresh per-run config + data dirs; `./dev cluster init` + `up`; wait for ready.
2. `keyval put/get` round trip on every node (stale-read polling per §10.8 discipline).
3. Two concurrent `keyval cas` against one version — exactly one success, one `version_mismatch` with the terminal-decision semantics verified via `keyval status`.
4. `keyval delete` (existed true/false), SCAN pagination across Unicode keys with `next_after` continuation.
5. Kill the leader mid-write burst (`./dev cluster kill`); use a bounded fixture that reliably leaves an unresolved request in `keyval pending`; `keyval resume` after restart resolves it with the SAME request ID and exact command. Both legal paths are tested: the earlier attempt committed and resume replays its original result, or it never committed and resume first-executes once. A subsequent same-ID retry/status returns the same first execution index/version, never a second execution.
6. Request-ID misuse: same ID + different command → `request_id_conflict`, nothing changed.
7. `./dev cluster down`; `keyval doctor` green on every stopped data directory.

## Registration
Registered in `registry/checks.toml` (tier t1, covers O-4, C-6, F-6, F-9 end-to-end; min_cases = the journey's step count) with its code marker — so T1 runs it hourly once implemented, per the W46 staging rules. Uses only public surfaces: the CLI, `./dev cluster`, HTTP status endpoints.

## Acceptance
The script passes against a fresh five-node cluster; each step emits a structured log record per the W01.6 standard, tee'd into the gate run's artifact directory; catchable interruption stops receipted processes, and uncatchable script termination leaves durable PID/config receipts that the outer gate harness or next invocation uses to stop only its owned processes (never promise SIGKILL runs cleanup handlers); the registry row resolves and executes with its min_cases.

## Area
`xtask` (script); separately reserve shared registry/checks.toml and output schema paths for registration; exercises `cli` and `server` as black boxes only.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.8 (stale-read discipline), §8.7, O-4, RISK-15, rule 12 (§11.5: register every new check).
acceptance_criteria:
Journey passes against a fresh 5-node cluster; every step logs action/expected/observed/duration per the W01.6 standard; resume-after-kill proves same-ID replay with no double execution; registry row resolves with min_cases; no stray processes
- [ ] Use deterministic public-surface preconditions for both executed-replay and never-executed-first-application resume paths; a timing-dependent leader kill that happens to lose no response cannot count as the unresolved-path assertion. Register the journey before W50, include its receipt in the M4 audit and preserve real CLI/HTTP-only assertions. Test catchable interruption and outer-harness cleanup after SIGKILL via owned PID receipts.
notes: This discovered check supplements the plan; it never changes the 53-item workgraph or activates O-4/C-6/F-6/F-9 through its own closure. Reserve xtask and shared registry/schema surfaces explicitly (§11.7).

title: BUG: gate and tests can run another checkout's build through the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR
description:
Context: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target comes from the tmux global environment (ACFS), so every keyval checkout on this box shares one target dir, including nested ones (`<target>/keyval-probes`, `keyval-probes-manual`, `keyval-scratch`). Cargo hashes path packages relative to the workspace root and judges freshness by mtime, and `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` (xtask/src/test_support.rs:10 `workspace_root`) is not part of the fingerprint. So a checkout whose sources are older than another checkout's last build reuses that build, with the other checkout's path baked in.

Observed 2026-10-03: main@459f437 `./dev gate fast` (receipt artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261003T141320Z-283675ab760c-1437177.json) ran the xtask test binary built 13:44 by the audit clone /data/projects/keyval-audit, so LINT-PROBES ran clippy against the audit clone's tree (an uncommitted-to-main `Instant::now` probe) and reported 19 false failures; "tests" counted 115 instead of 147. With a private target dir, and again after `cargo clean -p {types,xtask,lint-probe-production,lint-probe-deterministic}` in the shared dirs, the same tree passes 147 tests. The reverse direction is worse: a checkout can falsely PASS by running another tree's clean build. Gate receipts name a tree ID that the tests may not have run against (P11).

Risk to check: W07's `.local/candidate/` and `.local/accept/<tree-id>/` are further checkouts at different paths sharing the same target dir.

Requirements: P11 (exact-tree evidence), §11.10, §10.10, W01/W07 acceptance.
Area: xtask (./dev launcher, test_support.rs, gate/commit/accept target-dir handling).

Acceptance:
- Fixture: two checkouts of the same commit at different paths with one shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR; build a modified tree in checkout B, then `./dev gate fast` in checkout A tests A's sources (no diagnostics or results from B), and vice versa.
- `./dev` gate/commit/accept either use a per-checkout target dir (e.g. derived from the checkout's realpath) or prove the binaries under test were built from the receipt's tree; the receipt records the target dir used.
- No test locates the workspace via a compile-time path that can outlive its checkout.

Out of scope: changing the machine-wide CARGO_TARGET_DIR (ACFS-managed).
close_reason: Fixed in 665e60c (tree 06abad96); committed-tree gate receipt gate-fast-20261003T153116Z-06abad967f61-1673248 passed (158 tests, ubs clean, ast-grep rules_ran=true); details in comment

comments.author: charlie
comments.text:
Resolution (EmeraldCoyote): one target directory per checkout.

- `./dev` launcher: the shared base (CARGO_TARGET_DIR, else <root>/target) goes into KEYVAL_TARGET_BASE. CARGO_TARGET_DIR becomes `<base>/keyval-checkout-<first 16 hex of sha256(realpath of root)>`. Nested launchers derive from KEYVAL_TARGET_BASE, so nothing compounds. Every cargo run below ./dev inherits it, including the build of xtask itself, which was also exposed: a checkout could run another checkout's gate binary.
- xtask/src/cargo.rs: `target_base` and `checkout_target_dir` compute the same name in Rust. A unit test runs the real launcher with a fake cargo and checks that the two agree, that two checkouts sharing CARGO_TARGET_DIR get different dirs, that nested runs don't compound, and that a symlinked spelling maps to the same dir.
- W07 `.local/candidate/` (xtask/src/commit.rs `gate_command`): the candidate's gate now always builds into `checkout_target_dir(base, candidate)`. Before, it used `.local/candidate-target` only when CARGO_TARGET_DIR was unset. Under ACFS it is always set, so the candidate shared /data/tmp/cargo-target with every checkout. Unit test: `commit::tests::the_candidate_gate_builds_into_the_candidates_own_target_dir`.
- `.local/accept/<tree-id>/`: `./dev accept` does not exist yet (later W07 subtask). When it lands it must run cargo with `cargo::checkout_target_dir(&cargo::target_base(root), accept_dir)`, as commit.rs does. Note that every new accept path then costs a cold build and about 470 MB of target dir, so W46's prune of accept trees should prune their target dirs too.
- Receipts record `tools.cargo_target_dir`. Schemas bumped: keyval.dev.receipt/v2, keyval.dev.gate/v2 (rule 14). The receipt test asserts the field.
- No test locates the workspace through a compile-time path any more. Every `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` in xtask (test_support, gate, lint, check, workspace, metadata, tests/check.rs, tests/doctor.rs) now reads the runtime CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR that `cargo test` sets. (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask")` remains. It names the binary inside this checkout's own target dir, not the workspace.)

Acceptance fixture (manual, too heavy for T0; my scratchpad dtqu-fixture/):
- Two checkouts of tree 4cbc306e20e1 (= 459f437 + beads 1–2 paths) at different paths, one shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR. B adds a test `clock::only_in_checkout_b` that fails (tree 8d64c76306e0). B's files are newer than A's.
- Bug reproduced with the old launcher's behaviour (`cargo run` with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=shared): after B's gate, A's gate FAILED with "1 test(s) failed: clock::only_in_checkout_b::only_in_checkout_b", a test A does not contain. A had run B's build.
- With the fixed `./dev`, same shared base: B first, failed with its own test (target keyval-checkout-c0aadf6b9839f569). Then A passed, 153 tests, zero mentions of only_in_checkout_b in tests.log (target keyval-checkout-3ab90700d0a40cf8). Then B again: B's own result again (failed, only_in_checkout_b), so A's build never leaks into B.
- The A run is also a full gate for tree 4cbc306e: fmt, clippy, LINT-ALLOWS, LINT-TIERS, DEP-RULE, DEP-LEDGER, 153 tests, UBS on all 27 sources: passed.

Operational notes: the first `./dev` run in each checkout is a cold build (about 1 min, about 470 MB). The coordinator's pre-W07 flow, `.local/bootstrap-candidates/<tree>`, now costs that per commit (30 such dirs exist). It should materialise into one fixed directory instead.

title: BUG: gate counts a UBS run whose ast-grep rules never ran as passed
description:
Context: from at least 2026-09-30 02:04 until 2026-10-03 ~14:10, `ast-grep` on PATH was ~/.local/bin/ast-grep, a misnamed copy of ast-grep's `sg` deprecation shim that spawns `ast-grep` from PATH, i.e. itself, until fork fails with EAGAIN at the cgroup pids cap. Every cold UBS scan therefore ran none of its ast-grep rules, yet UBS exited 0 with `status: ok` and `failed_modules: []`, and the gate recorded "ubs passed". The same loop exhausted the M0 auditor agent's pids cap (TasksMax=3644) and it aborted (SIGABRT) mid-audit at 13:46:36. The shim was moved aside on 2026-10-03 (~/.local/bin/ast-grep.sg-shim.bak) and the UBS cache from that period moved to ~/.cache/ubs-pre-shim-fix-20261003; the environment is fixed, but the gate still cannot tell a partial UBS scan from a clean one.

Consequence: every UBS "passed" receipt before 2026-10-03 14:13 (including W01's final acceptance and W07.1) is a partial scan. The first full scan is artifacts/receipts/gate-fast-20261003T142021Z-283675ab760c-1445981.json (UBS red; see the UBS-vs-CD-8 conflict bug).

Requirements: §10.10 (UBS in the gate fast set), O-8, W01 acceptance (doctor capability probes).
Area: xtask (gate.rs UBS step, doctor.rs ubs/ast-grep probes).

Acceptance:
- Fixture: with a failing `ast-grep` first on PATH (exits non-zero, or a self-spawning stub under a small pids cap), `./dev gate fast` fails the UBS step instead of passing.
- `./dev doctor` runs a bounded real ast-grep query (not just `--version`) and fails on such a stub.
- The gate receipt records which ast-grep binary/version UBS used and that its rules ran.

Out of scope: fixing UBS's exit status upstream; the shim installer (report separately to UBS/ACFS).
close_reason: Fixed in 665e60c (tree 06abad96); committed-tree gate receipt gate-fast-20261003T153116Z-06abad967f61-1673248 passed (158 tests, ubs clean, ast-grep rules_ran=true); details in comment

comments.author: charlie
comments.text:
Resolution (EmeraldCoyote).

Root cause, measured with UBS 5.4.17 using `--no-cache`, on a file holding one production panic!:
- With ast-grep absent from PATH: status ok, exit 0, 0 criticals. The Rust module checks only `command -v ast-grep` and silently skips every ast-grep rule.
- With a stub that exits 1, or one that exits 0 and prints nothing, first on PATH: also status ok, exit 0, 0 criticals.
- UBS's scan cache is keyed by file content, not by the ast-grep that produced an entry. A hit can therefore replay a hollow scan, and with a warm cache the broken stubs still "found" the panic.

Fix (xtask/src/gate.rs `ubs_step`):
1. Canary. Every UBS step first scans a canary file (`UBS_CANARY`: one production panic!, which only the ast-grep rule pack detects). It requires exactly 1 critical and exit 1 (`canary_verdict`). Otherwise the step fails with "UBS did not report the canary's panic!, so its ast-grep rules did not run", and stops before passes 1–2, whose results would be meaningless.
2. Every gate UBS run uses `--no-cache` (measured cost: 12.3 s vs 12.0 s on 27 files).
3. Each pass must report every given file as scanned (added with br-gate-ubs-test-panics-brzy).
4. Receipt `tools.ast_grep = {path, version, rules_ran}`: the ast-grep on UBS's PATH, its `--version` line (or why it failed), and whether the canary proved its rules ran. Covered by the receipt/v2 bump from br-gate-shared-target-dir-dtqu.
5. `./dev doctor` lists ast-grep as required. Its capability probe is a real, bounded query (`ast-grep run --lang rust --pattern 'mod $NAME;' --json=compact xtask/src/main.rs`, under doctor's 30 s limit) that must return a JSON array with ≥1 real match.

Tests (all run in T0):
- `gate::tests::ubs_fails_when_its_ast_grep_rules_do_not_run`: the real UBS, with a failing ast-grep stub and then a silent one first on PATH. The step fails on the canary, and the receipt names the stub, its version outcome and rules_ran=false.
- `gate::tests::canary_verdicts`.
- `gate::tests::ubs_lets_tests_panic_but_never_production_code` now also asserts rules_ran=true with the real ast-grep.
- `doctor::tests::the_ast_grep_query_must_return_real_matches` (failing, silent, deprecation text, `[]`, lookalike JSON).
- `doctor::tests::the_installed_ast_grep_answers_the_real_query`.
- `tests/doctor.rs::an_ast_grep_that_matches_nothing_fails_doctor`: a fake whose --version works but whose query prints nothing.

Self-spawning stub (the real incident shim, a copy of ~/.local/bin/ast-grep.sg-shim.bak named ast-grep, first on PATH). Run by hand, only under `systemd-run --user --scope -p TasksMax=40`, never in the test suite:
- `xtask --json doctor`: ast-grep status "broken" (`ast-grep --version` exited 1).
- `xtask gate fast` on the gate-ubs fixture: the ubs step FAILED with "canary: UBS did not report the canary's panic!, so its ast-grep rules did not run …". The receipt has tools.ast_grep = {path: <stub>, version: "`ast-grep --version` exited with exit status: 1", rules_ran: false}.

Evidence for the combined tree 06abad967f61 (459f437 + all three beads' paths), frozen, git-isolated candidate:
- `./dev gate fast --changed …`: passed (158 tests, ubs 14 files).
- Full UBS scan: passed. Canary 1 critical (expected), pass 1 0 critical / 27 files, pass 2 0 critical / 23 production views. Receipt: ast_grep /home/charlie/.cargo/bin/ast-grep 0.45.3, rules_ran true.
- This gate also caught a real issue in my first draft: rust.security.command-executable on `Command::new(<looked-up path>)`, fixed to a fixed program name resolved on the child's PATH.

Not done (out of scope): UBS upstream (its Rust module should mark a scan partial when ast-grep is missing or fails, and its cache key should include the ast-grep identity), and the shim installer.

comments.text: Owner decision 2026-10-03: CD-8 wins (tests may use unwrap/expect/panic!). comments.author: charlie
comments.text:
Resolution (EmeraldCoyote, per the owner's CD-8 decision above; policy files untouched):

The gate's UBS step now runs two passes (xtask/src/gate.rs `ubs_step`):
1. The exact changed files, every UBS rule except category `rust.ownership` (`--skip=rust.ownership`).
2. A production view of the same Rust files, every rule. In this view, test code is blanked to spaces, with line numbers kept (`lint::production_view`). Test code is what clippy's allow-panic-in-tests means: `#[test]` and `#[cfg(test)]` items, and `#![cfg(test)]` scopes, which every tests/*.rs file starts with. The views are kept next to the receipt under `gate-<run>/ubs-production/`.

Why: UBS 5.4.17's Rust module drops its per-finding records from every machine format (JSON, JSONL and SARIF carry only counts). So the gate cannot tell which rule or location a critical came from. `rust.ownership`'s only critical rule is `rust.ownership.panic-macro`. Its other rules (unwrap/expect, todo!, unimplemented!, unreachable!, dbg!, println!) are warnings or infos, which never fail the gate. Net effect: only `panic!` inside test code stops failing the gate, and production code still faces every rule. Rejected: `ubs:ignore[rust.ownership.panic-macro]` markers on test lines, because UBS's statement-interval semantics let a marker on the line above a statement suppress it, so a production panic! right after a test item could be hidden. Also rejected: the Rust module's own `--exclude-tests`, which the meta-runner does not forward, and which drops every rule in test code, using a boundary heuristic UBS itself calls permissive.

Each pass is judged by its `--report-json` (status, failed_modules, criticals, exit code). It must also report every given file as scanned, otherwise it is a partial scan and fails. The text report goes to ubs.log, so the log shows the panic rule ran ("No panic! macros" in pass 2) and where any finding is.

Evidence (pre-commit, my frozen git-isolated candidate = 459f437 + the paths below, tree c44e7f3e85772133d4ac177da18109e528b890cc, private CARGO_TARGET_DIR):
- `./dev gate fast --changed <paths>`: passed, 150 tests, ubs 2 files.
- `./dev gate fast` with no --changed (UBS on all 27 first-party sources, as on the red main receipt): passed. Pass 1: 0 critical / 27 files. Pass 2: 0 critical / 23 production views.
- Probe `gate::tests::ubs_lets_tests_panic_but_never_production_code` uses the real UBS on fixture xtask/tests/fixtures/gate-ubs. The step fails with exactly "pass 2 (production code): UBS found 1 critical issue(s)" at src/halve.rs:7:9 [rule:rust.ownership.panic-macro]. The test panics at src/lib.rs:18 (#[cfg(test)]) and tests/doubling.rs:6 (#![cfg(test)]) are not flagged.
The official receipt will come from the coordinator's commit run.

title: W02.1x: RAFT-VENDOR check, ./dev doctor probe and build_id input for the vendored Raft library
description:
## Context
W02.1 vendored raft and raft-proto 0.7.0 under vendor/raft/ and pinned code generation by vendoring raft-proto's generated eraftpb code: build = false, so no protoc runs at build time. Provenance and every file's sha256 are in vendor/raft/VENDOR.toml. The xtask half of W02.1 is split out here, because xtask/** was reserved for W07 when W02.1 ran: the executable check, the ./dev doctor probe, and the explicit build_id input. W02.1 closes with accept:RAFT-VENDOR once this lands.

## Requirements
P4, T-3 ("same build" covers generated-code provenance, pinned protoc), T-11; PLAN §7.3, §12.2 W02.

## Area
xtask: a new leaf module plus a catalogue row in check.rs, doctor.rs and gate.rs build inputs. These are xtask facades, so they need a short reservation.

## Design
1. Static check RAFT-VENDOR (catalogue row; marker; covers P4, T-3; class invariant; tier T0; min_cases = the files listed in VENDOR.toml, 73 today). It fails when:
   - VENDOR.toml is missing, or its schema is not keyval.vendor.raft/v1;
   - any vendored file is missing, unlisted, or has a sha256 different from [crate.files];
   - a [codegen].outputs entry is not a listed file;
   - raft-proto/Cargo.toml has build != false, any build-dependencies, or a prost/protobuf-build dependency or feature;
   - raft does not resolve raft-proto via path = "../raft-proto";
   - raft-proto's protobuf requirement is not "=<[codegen].protobuf_runtime>";
   - the root Cargo.lock contains protobuf-build or protobuf-codegen, or contains protobuf at a version other than the runtime.
   Negative fixtures for each of these. A reference implementation of the same assertions, used as W02.1's evidence, is described in the bead thread.
2. ./dev doctor probe 'raft-codegen-pin': runs the RAFT-VENDOR assertions (cheap, file hashing only) and reports the pinned protoc (libprotoc 3.9.0, sha256 from VENDOR.toml). It fails if vendor/raft exists and the check fails; once W02.1 has landed it also fails if vendor/raft is missing.
3. build_id: add raft_vendor_sha256 (sha256 of vendor/raft/VENDOR.toml) to BuildInputs and the build_id preimage, beside raft_patch_sha256. The receipt then shows codegen provenance explicitly; bump the receipt schema version (O-6).

## Acceptance
./dev check RAFT-VENDOR passes on the committed tree and executes >= min_cases; every negative fixture fails as specified; ./dev check DEV-DOCTOR covers the new probe (pass and fail); DEV-GATE covers the new build input; then add the accept:RAFT-VENDOR label to br-w02-1-vendor-pin-protoc-wqi.

## Out of scope
Changing vendored files; the entropy patch (W02.3); any workspace consumer of raft (W02.4 / W13).

title: M0: Foundations — workspace, gates, spec, spike, registry, commit protocol
description:
## What this milestone delivers
A working development substrate before any database code exists: the `./dev` entry point (a Rust xtask behind a thin launcher) with `doctor`, `check` and `gate fast`; the pinned toolchain and lint policy; AGENTS.md with the normative agent rules; DEPENDENCIES.md; the OpenAPI contract; the Raft determinism spike; domain types and ports; the validated config type with genesis fingerprint; the verification registry and its T0 gate; the work-graph manifest and idempotent bead importer; and the exact-candidate commit wrapper.

Items: W01–W08. M0 exists so that *everything later is verifiable from the first real commit*: gates, receipts, registry traceability and the commit protocol are in place before the first line of consensus or storage code lands.

## Why this ordering
The project's primary goal (G1) is to exercise the agentic development flywheel — plan → beads → parallel agents → mechanical gates → human review of outputs, not code. Nobody reviews code by hand (D-17), so the mechanical quality bar (lints, registry gate, exact-tree commits) must exist *before* the swarm starts. The Raft spike (W02) is the highest-risk item in the whole plan (RISK-1) and runs here, in parallel, so a no-go is discovered before anything is built on the library.

## Bootstrap process constraint
Until W07 (commit wrapper) lands, ALL commits go through a single coordinator agent which stages, runs the bootstrap gate on a frozen candidate copy, and commits; other agents code in parallel and hand files to the coordinator. The full self-serve swarm launches only once W04 + W06 + W07 have all landed.

## Owner checkpoint (after M0)
The owner runs `./dev doctor`, reads the API examples in `api/openapi.yaml`, and looks at `bv` and the list of `planned` checks. No database is advertised yet.

## Process guardrails (apply to every bead in this epic)
- Commits only via `./dev commit` once W07 exists; never raw `git add`/`git commit`; never branches/worktrees (D-16: all agents share `main`).
- Oracles are sacred (P9): never weaken a checker, test, fixture, golden file or corpus seed to get green.
- Evidence over claims (P5): close beads only with passing acceptance receipts; state claims in their class (§10.15).
- Precedence (§0.4): owner > PLAN.md > openapi.yaml > checkers/model/registry > tests > beads > code. If this bead text and PLAN.md ever disagree, PLAN.md wins — file a `conflict` bead, never silently pick a side.

Plan refs: PLAN.md §11.2, §12.1, §17; decisions D-15, D-16, D-17, D-32.

title: M1: Thin durable slice — durable PUT/GET on a real node and a simulated 5-node cluster
description:
## What this milestone delivers
The first runnable, honest slice of keyval: durable PUT/GET through the *real* Raft core — once as a single real node over HTTP (`keyval-server`), and once as a simulated five-node cluster with crash-restart — plus the beginnings of the verification stack (reference model, simulation scheduler, canonical trace, fresh-process replay).

Items: W09–W20 (state machine, reference model, journal, byte-storage adapters, raft-rs adapter + Ready loop, node controller, sim scheduler/network/composition root, production composition root, M1 demo, M1 drift audit).

## Why a thin slice first
D-40: the earliest runnable evidence must exercise *every* layer — HTTP boundary, controller, consensus, journal, recovery, simulation and determinism — before any breadth (DELETE/CAS/SCAN) is added. A convincing simulation without a real durable server is not acceptable, and neither is the reverse (P6: real slices only; no stub presented as the real thing).

## The two stop/go points live here
W13 (the Ready loop over raft-rs) is the second technical stop/go point after the W02 spike. The Ready loop (§7.4) is THE critical persistence protocol: entries, term and vote must be synced before any dependent message leaves the node; getting this ordering wrong is the classic way replicated systems lose acknowledged data (RISK-2).

## Determinism is non-negotiable from M1 on
Same seed + same build ⇒ byte-identical canonical trace, in fresh OS processes (P4, T-3, T-11). Any nondeterminism found later is a P0. The simulator runs the same state machine, Raft adapter and journal code as production (P3) — only adapters differ.

## Owner checkpoint (demo m1)
`./dev demo m1`: one real node, PUT and GET, kill and restart it, read the key back; `./dev sim run --seed 42 --profile slice` twice with identical trace hashes.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic (commit wrapper, P9 oracle protection, claim classes, §0.4 precedence). From M1 on, verification work (tracks D/E) runs in parallel with product work — it is never bolted on at the end.

Plan refs: PLAN.md §12.1, §11.6; decisions D-28, D-40; risks RISK-2, RISK-6.

title: M2: Real cluster — five processes, routing, launcher, doctor, crash probes
description:
## What this milestone delivers
Five *real* OS processes forming a cluster on one machine: peer transport over HTTP, write routing (307 redirect to leader / 503 with node list), the `./dev cluster` launcher with PID receipts, the `keyval doctor` offline data-directory verifier, and the real-file process-crash probes + five-node lifecycle smoke test.

Items: W21–W26 (peer transport & routing, cluster launcher, CLI doctor, crash probes & smoke, M2 demo, M2 drift audit).

## Why this matters
Simulated bytes cannot prove that the real file adapter drives real files correctly (D-33). M2 closes the loop between the simulated world of M1 and physical processes: SIGKILL at defined write/sync boundaries, restart from the real data directory, and verification that every acknowledged write survived. Note the honest limit: SIGKILL does not drop the OS page cache, so these are *process-crash* probes, not power-loss tests; power-loss durability is a stated Assumption (D-46), partially covered by the sync-order check at the syscall boundary.

## Safety rules for real processes
The launcher records PID receipts and only ever signals processes it started; it never kills by port, never uses broad pkill, and never deletes data. Destructive re-initialisation is a separate, explicit owner action outside every gate (O-2). A node that lost its data directory must REFUSE to start blank — silent re-join is Raft amnesia and can lose committed entries (D-52).

## Owner checkpoint (demo m2)
`./dev demo m2`: a 5-node local cluster; the owner kills and restarts nodes by hand including the leader; watches `/v1/cluster`; runs `keyval doctor` on a stopped node's data directory.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic. Manage nodes only through `./dev cluster …` (AGENTS.md rule 18).

Plan refs: PLAN.md §12.1, §10.17, §11.6; decisions D-33, D-46, D-52.

title: M3: Full product surface — DELETE/CAS/SCAN/status, full API, CLI, conformance
description:
## What this milestone delivers
The complete product surface: DELETE, COMPARE_SWAP, SCAN, request-status lookup, the full retry/ambiguity lifecycle (attach, conflict, history_full, capacity_exceeded), the complete HTTP API passing an independent conformance suite, the reference model server, and the full `keyval` CLI with its durable pending store.

Items: W27–W35 (DELETE/CAS, SCAN, request status & retry lifecycle, model server, conformance suite, complete HTTP surface, full CLI, M3 demo, M3 drift audit).

## The semantic heart of keyval
Retry safety never expires: every write carries a client 128-bit Idempotency-Key; its first execution (log index, command digest, terminal result) is replicated state for the life of the cluster (DM-5, D-07). A CAS mismatch and a live-quota capacity_exceeded are *committed terminal decisions* that consume the request ID — they prove execution exactly like a success (§9.3). Unknown outcomes are first-class, never guessed (P8).

## Independence discipline
The conformance suite (W31) and reference model server (W30) depend on NO production crate and talk only HTTP (T-12). Semantic tests must pass against the model server *before* the real server is complete — this validates the suite and the spec independently, and is why suite and server can be built in parallel by different agents (§11.7 independent authorship).

## Owner checkpoint (demo m3)
`./dev demo m3`: two clients contend with CAS on one version; paginate Unicode keys; replay a request ID; resolve an unknown_outcome with `keyval status` and `keyval resume`.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic. W32's closure is the single switch that turns registry spec↔code/spec↔tests conditions from report-mode to enforcing (D-49).

Plan refs: PLAN.md §12.1, §8, §7.8, §10.8; decisions D-07, D-35, D-36, D-54.

title: M4: Evidence — checkers, swarm campaigns, bug injection, gates, crash packs
description:
## What this milestone delivers
The full evidence machine: workload generator, nemesis and swarm fault campaigns with coverage accounting, all fourteen checkers (K-1…K-14), non-vacuity enforcement, crash packs and scenario shrinking, the bug-injection checker self-test (B-01…B-22), staged gate tiers T0–T3 with receipts and the failure outbox, parity checks, fuzzing and code-coverage reporting, measurements, and the `./dev status` owner view.

Items: W36–W50 plus W53 (workload, nemesis/swarm/heal, checkers, non-vacuity+coverage, sim commands+crash packs, full-op profiles, shrinker, bug variants, gate tiers+scheduler, measurements, parity, status view, fuzz+coverage, M4 drift audit).

## The philosophy being exercised
Evidence over claims (P5): every MUST requirement has a registered, executed check; every claim carries its class — invariant / simulation-evidenced / measurement / assumption / proposal (§10.15). A weaker class never justifies a stronger claim: "no violation in 100,000 seeds on build X" is evidence, never "keyval is linearizable". No vacuous passes (P10): a zero-test selection, an unexercised fault, an exhausted budget or an incomplete campaign FAILS. Checkers are themselves checked: deliberately injected bugs must be caught by their designated checker, with the unmutated control passing (§10.6) — the mechanical guard against agents weakening oracles to get green (RISK-3).

## Parallelism note
M4 work starts as soon as its dependencies land (from M1 onwards); it runs in parallel with M2 and M3. Milestones are views over work items, not phases.

## Owner checkpoint (M4 review — reports, not a demo)
The owner opens a crash pack from the corpus, replays and shrinks it; reads the bug-variant report, coverage matrix and measurements; checks `./dev status`.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic. Every failing case fixed goes into `sim/corpus/` in the same commit (AGENTS.md rule 9); the corpus is append-only (P9).

Plan refs: PLAN.md §10 (whole section), §12.1; decisions D-14, D-22, D-23, D-24, D-34, D-66, D-67.

title: M5: v1 — clean-state rehearsal, T3 release campaign, Definition of Done
description:
## What this milestone delivers
v1 itself: the final (M5) drift audit, the clean-state rehearsal (fresh clone → doctor → build → cluster init+up → smoke), the T3 release campaign (≥ 100,000 fresh swarm seeds, 100 fresh-process replay pairs, every bug variant, required coverage cells), and the Definition-of-Done reconciliation with the final evidence report.

Items: W51, W52.

## Definition of Done (condensed from §13)
1. Five-node system starts from one config, exposes API/CLI/status, persists real bytes, recovers without operator repair. 2. Every MUST requirement active and passed on the release build; registry gate green. 3. T3: 0 violations over ≥100k seeds, every required coverage cell non-zero, no incomplete runs; the release build is the exact tree T3 ran on (D-58). 4. Every bug variant caught, control passing. 5. Determinism self-check clean (100 replay pairs). 6. Conformance 100% vs model server, real single node and 5-node cluster. 7. Crash probes + lifecycle smoke + parity pass. 8. T0 enforced on every commit; a scheduled failure demonstrably becomes exactly one bead even across a tracker outage. 9. Measurements report generated. 10. No open P0 beads, no open P1 BUG beads (W51/W52 orchestration beads exempt while they run), no open conflict beads, no unanswered owner disposition. 11. Owner checkpoints M1–M5 complete; drift audits complete with no finding above P2 open. 12. All 53 work items closed with acceptance receipts. 13. Decision log up to date. 14. Final evidence report states every claim in its correct class.

Not required: human code review, hosted CI, performance numbers. A complete implementation with missing evidence is not v1; a convincing simulation without a real durable server is not v1 either.

## Sequencing rule (D-73)
The final audit runs BEFORE the T3 campaign (inside W51). A code-changing finding discovered after the campaign spawns a new release-campaign bead and T3 re-runs on the new tree — evidence is never silently carried across trees.

## Process guardrails
Same as M0's epic.

Plan refs: PLAN.md §13, §10.10 (T3), §10.11, §11.9; decisions D-58, D-73.

title: Tie api/openapi.yaml error consts to their enums; fix review findings in the W03.1/W03.2 spec
description:
## Context
Fresh-eyes review of api/openapi.yaml (W03.1 0fdee5e, W03.2 6093b06) by its author. No contract change; consistency and clarity only.

## Findings
1. `ErrorCode` and `AttemptState` are orphaned: every error schema hard-codes `code: {const}` and `attempt_state: {const}` without referencing the enum, so nothing checks that each per-code schema's code is one of the twelve §8.4 codes (the input to §10.13 condition 5). `ReadyHealth.lifecycle` and `NotReadyLifecycle` likewise restate lifecycle values without tying them to `Lifecycle`.
2. The Errors section says the details schema depends on read vs write only for busy/unavailable/recovering; `invalid_request` has read and write variants too.
3. The response component `SetCapacity` reads as a verb; it is the PUT/CAS 507 set, so rename it `VersionedWriteCapacity` (matching `VersionedWriteResult`). Nothing outside the file references it yet.

## Requirements
F-8, F-10, §8.4, §10.13 condition 5.

## Area
api (api/openapi.yaml, shared surface, short reservation).

## Acceptance
Each error schema's `code` and `attempt_state` add a `$ref` to `ErrorCode`/`AttemptState` beside the `const`, and the lifecycle fields reference `Lifecycle`. No component is left unreferenced. The spec still validates as OpenAPI 3.1, and the scratch W03.1/W03.2 instance checks still pass. T0 is green on the exact tree.

## Out of scope
Owner readings (W03.1/W03.2 comments), br-s4dg, the SPEC check (W03.3).

description:
## Context

title: Closure gap: a subtask whose acceptance check lands in a later split-off bead's commit cannot close (W02.1 / br-gqxq)
description:
## Context
`./dev commit --close <bead>` (W07.3; xtask/src/closure.rs work_commit and validate) requires the newest passing accept receipt to name the tree of the newest main commit whose message carries `Bead: <bead>`. W02.1 (br-w02-1-vendor-pin-protoc-wqi) had its xtask half split into br-gqxq because xtask/** was reserved for W07 at the time. W02.1's work commit is 07e9ec7 (tree 8c72e61a, which vendors raft). Its acceptance check, RAFT-VENDOR, only exists from br-gqxq's commit 79de0e8 (tree 3114abd4). So:
- `./dev accept br-w02-1-vendor-pin-protoc-wqi --tree 8c72e61a…` cannot select RAFT-VENDOR, which does not exist in that tree. It fails, as P10 requires.
- An accept receipt on 3114abd4 is refused by --close as 'wrong tree' (P11).
W02.1 therefore cannot close through the wrapper, and W02.2 → W02.3 → W02.4 → W02.5 → W02 (critical-path risk item; W13 depends on it) stay blocked. br-gqxq itself is unaffected: its work commit carries its own check.

## Requirements
P11, §11.3 step 7, §11.4 (closing needs a receipt for the tree that carried the work), rule 16.

## Options (owner decision)
A. Owner override for W02.1 (§0.4 rule 1): close it with a bead comment citing br-gqxq's committed-tree gate receipt (gate-fast-20261003T164707Z-3114abd48aec-2169983) and an accept receipt for RAFT-VENDOR on 3114abd4.
B. A W02.1-trailer commit on top of 79de0e8. This needs genuine W02.1-scoped content; an empty commit would be gaming the rule, and ./dev commit presumably refuses one.
C. Convention for future splits, needing no code change: commits of a split-off bead also carry the parent subtask's trailer (`Bead: <split-off>` and `Bead: <parent>`). closure.rs already matches any `Bead:` line, so the parent's work tree becomes the one that contains its check. Document it in AGENTS.md. This does not help W02.1 retroactively.
D. A wrapper change (W07 area, plan-level): treat the newest commit of a bead that <bead> depends on, and that was split from it, as carrying <bead>'s work. This weakens the exact-tree rule's simplicity; not recommended.
Recommendation: A for W02.1 now, plus C going forward.

## Area
.beads (decision); AGENTS.md if C is adopted.

## Acceptance
W02.1 is closed with receipt-backed evidence the owner accepts, and W02.2 becomes ready. If C is adopted, AGENTS.md states the trailer convention for split-off beads.

## Out of scope
Rewriting history (amending 79de0e8 to add a trailer is forbidden).

title: BUG: PLAN.md's 2^53 integer boundary disagrees between §8.1 ('below' vs 'above 2^53') and §7.10 (node IDs '≤ 2^53')
description:
## Context
PLAN.md gives three different boundaries at exactly 2^53 for API integers. A boundary conformance test (2^53 - 1 / 2^53 / 2^53 + 1) and W08's config parser must agree with the spec, so the plan needs one rule.

## The conflicting locations
1. §8.1 Integers: "all validated **below** 2^53" (so 2^53 itself is invalid; max = 2^53 - 1 = 9007199254740991, which is also JavaScript's Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER).
2. §8.1, same bullet: "a CAS `expected.version` **above** 2^53 is `invalid_request`" (read literally, this leaves 2^53 itself unaddressed rather than invalid).
3. §7.10 Config validation: "node IDs must be nonzero and **≤ 2^53** (R-22)" (so a node ID of exactly 2^53 is accepted at config parse, then reported in `served_by.node_id`, `/v1/cluster` and health, violating rule 1). W08's bead copies "≤ 2^53".

## What the spec does meanwhile
`api/openapi.yaml` (W03.1) follows the general §8.1 rule: every integer schema has `maximum: 9007199254740991`, and the conventions say a request integer at or above 2^53 is `400 invalid_request`. That is the reading where every reported integer is a safe JSON integer. If the owner picks "≤ 2^53" instead, the spec's maxima change to 9007199254740992.

## Requirements
§8.1, §7.10, R-22, F-5, O-5; W03, W08, W31 boundary tests.

## Area
PLAN.md (owner-owned): a plan-change to one wording, then api/openapi.yaml and W08 follow.

## Acceptance
The owner picks one boundary; §8.1 and §7.10 state it identically; api/openapi.yaml and W08's parser match it.

## Out of scope
Changing integer encoding (R-22 stays rejected).

In §8.1's integers bullet, "a CAS expected.version above 2^53" becomes "at or above 2^53", and "a term above 2^53" becomes "a term at or above 2^53" (same bullet, same rule). title: W01.6: Project-wide test logging & diagnostics standard
description:
Codify the project-wide TEST LOGGING & DIAGNOSTICS STANDARD, documented in AGENTS.md's Testing section and enforced from the first bead onward, so every later suite inherits it:

1. **Assertion context.** Every assertion message carries enough state to diagnose without a debugger: the CD-7 `invariant!` style (node, index, invariant ID) extends to ALL test suites — a failing test names the inputs, the expected value, the observed value and the rule violated.
2. **Re-runnability.** Property-test failures persist their seed and shrunk case, and the failure output contains the exact re-run command (mirroring the simulator's seed/replay discipline, T-4). A failing test you cannot re-run from its log is a defect.
3. **E2E/probe/demo step logging.** Every scripted end-to-end flow (demos in --assert mode, the lifecycle smoke, crash probes, parity scenario, clean-state rehearsal, the CLI journey) logs each step as a structured record — step name, action, expected, observed, outcome, duration — to stderr AND a log file in the run's artifact directory, and exits non-zero on the first failed step. Gate runs tee these logs next to their receipts.
4. **No silent skips.** A skipped step or vacuous selection is logged as such and fails per P10.
5. **Bounded.** Test logs respect CD-9 (bounded size; oldest-dropped-and-counted) and the Q9 .local/ retention rule (pruned only by ./dev prune).
6. **Helpers stay out of production.** Any shared logging helper is a dev-dependency/test-support module only, never compiled into production builds (T-6 discipline), and never logs from inside deterministic-core production paths (the canonical trace and Telemetry port own those).

Acceptance: the standard is written into AGENTS.md's Testing section; a minimal test-support helper exists where it pays; W01's probe tests demonstrate a failing test producing a context-rich, re-runnable log record. Part of W01.

title: W01: Bootstrap workspace, pinned toolchain, ./dev (doctor/check/gate fast), lint policy, AGENTS.md, DEPENDENCIES.md, beads init
description:
## Context
Everything in this project flows through one repo-owned entry point: `./dev` (a Rust xtask behind a small launcher). W01 creates the workspace, the pinned toolchain, the lint policy that substitutes for human code review, the AGENTS.md rulebook, DEPENDENCIES.md, and the first (bootstrap) gate — before any database code exists. Local verification is the authority (P7): there is no hosted CI; every gate is a command on the dev machine that writes a receipt.

## Requirements covered
- P7 (local verification is the authority), CD-8 (no unwrap/expect/panic/todo/unimplemented/unsafe in first-party production code), CD-12 (every dependency justified in DEPENDENCIES.md; lockfile committed), O-8 (`./dev status` / `./dev doctor` surface — doctor part here).

## Area (file reservations)
`root` (workspace Cargo.toml/lock, rust-toolchain.toml, dev launcher, AGENTS.md, DEPENDENCIES.md, .gitignore), `xtask`.

## Depends on
Nothing — this is the first item. Until W07 lands, only the coordinator agent commits (bootstrap exception, §11.2 step 2).

## Design & key rules
- `./dev doctor`: probes the environment — toolchain, br, bv, NTM, UBS, DCG, Agent Mail — records each installed version, and FAILS on a missing capability (never assumes documented behaviour; RISK-16).
- `./dev check <ID>`: unknown IDs and zero-test selections fail (P10 — no vacuous passes).
- `./dev gate fast` (bootstrap form): runs a FIXED set until the registry (W05) takes over: format check, lints with denied warnings, dependency-rule check, xtask unit tests, UBS on staged files. Writes a receipt with the tree ID.
- Lint policy (enforces §5.2 mechanically, because nobody reviews code — D-17): `unsafe_code` forbidden; `unwrap_used`/`expect_used`/`panic`/`todo`/`unimplemented` denied outside tests; wildcard enum match arms denied in deterministic crates (CD-5); missing docs denied on public items in deterministic crates (CD-11); determinism lints (no `Instant::now`/`SystemTime::now`, no thread/async spawns, no randomly-hashed maps in deterministic crates — §7.14). Lints are pinned to the project toolchain and PROVEN effective: a probe file that violates each lint must be rejected (never assume a lint works from its docs).
- The project `invariant!` macro (built on `assert!`) is the only sanctioned panic path (CD-7/CD-8), so bare `panic!` stays denied without allowing any CD-enforcing or determinism lint. Any unrelated narrow allow must satisfy the documented escape-hatch policy and bead decision log in AGENTS.md.
- AGENTS.md carries the 18 normative rules of §11.5 (owner override; §0.4 precedence + `conflict` beads; P9 oracle protection; determinism; hexagonal core; real slices only; plan is owner-owned; stay in your area; seeds to corpus; robot mode; CD rules; registry discipline; claim classes; JSON schemas; `./dev commit` only — no raw git, no branches/worktrees, no `ntm --worktrees`; receipts as the only evidence; test-only code gating; node-data safety). It must state explicitly that this project REPLACES the ACFS landing-the-plane git checklist.
- DEPENDENCIES.md: every direct dependency with purpose, scope, version, licence, source. Deterministic crates start from std + vendored raft only.

## Acceptance
- `./dev doctor` reports every required tool with its version and fails when one is missing.
- `./dev check NOPE` fails.
- `./dev gate fast` runs the bootstrap set on the clean workspace and writes a receipt containing the tree ID.
- A probe file using `unwrap` outside tests is rejected by the lint gate.
- AGENTS.md contains every §11.5 rule.

## Out of scope
The verification registry and registry-driven gate staging (W05); the commit wrapper (W07); any server/db code; beads import (W06). Do not create empty placeholder crates (P6) — crates are created by the first bead that needs them.

## Notes for the future
- Budget target for T0 is ≤ 2 min warm with a 3-min alert threshold; keep the bootstrap gate lean from day one (RISK-19: serialised commits make T0 latency the commit throughput bound).
- UBS is pinned for gate runs; auto-update disabled during verification; partial scan = failure.

PLAN.md wins over this bead on any disagreement (§0.4) — file a `conflict` bead. Plan refs: §11.1, §11.5, §11.13, §10.10, §5.2.

title: W02: Raft library determinism spike — vendor, audit, entropy patch, fresh-process proof, go/no-go
description:
## Context
Decision 1 of the whole plan: prove the deterministic consensus boundary FIRST, before building anything on it. We borrow Raft rather than writing it (D-05, R-02): primary is TiKV `raft-rs` (`raft` + `raft-proto` 0.7.0, last release Mar 2023 — RISK-1), a consensus-module-only library the application drives via tick/step/propose/Ready/advance, which fits a discrete-event simulator naturally. But it randomises election timeouts internally and may hide other nondeterminism; P4 demands: same seed + same build ⇒ byte-identical traces across fresh OS processes. This spike vendors, audits, patches and PROVES that, with an explicit go/no-go.

## Requirements covered
P4 (determinism), T-3 (byte-identical canonical trace), T-11 (fresh-process replay identity).

## Area
`vendor` (vendor/raft/, third_party/raft.patch), `spike` (spike/ — kept as evidence).

## Depends on
W01 (workspace, toolchain, gate).

## Design & key rules
- Vendor `raft`/`raft-proto` 0.7.0 into `vendor/raft/` with recorded checksums, enabled features, toolchain.
- AUDIT: enumerate every path reachable from construction, campaign, tick, step and timeout reset that could introduce nondeterminism — entropy, ambient clocks, threads, unordered collection iteration, randomly seeded hashers, pointer formatting, logging side effects. Also enumerate unbounded entry fetches on election/commit paths (e.g. `maybe_commit_by_vote` materialising entries with no size limit); each finding gets a bounded-handling policy (W13 adds the large-log test). Unproven "probably fine" items get a test.
- PATCH (`third_party/raft.patch`): minimal; routes every randomness source — notably randomised election timeouts at construction and on every reset — through a MANDATORY, self-contained entropy trait defined INSIDE the vendored crate (D-57: the vendored crate never depends on first-party code; upstream tests supply a seeded source; no ambient default). The patch MUST NOT touch vote, log-matching, quorum or commit rules. Setting a timeout from outside after construction is NOT sufficient (reset paths re-randomise).
- Codegen pinning: `PROTOC` forced to a bundled binary, or the generated code vendored, so no PATH-dependent protoc can vary the build; recorded in `build_id`; checked by `./dev doctor`.
- Determinism proof: a seeded 3-node in-memory loop gives identical spike-local traces for 100 seeds × 3 fresh processes, including crash-restart and re-election.

## Acceptance
- Vendored 0.7.0 with checksums; audit report lists every finding with its policy; the patch defines and injects the vendored entropy trait; upstream tests pass with the patch; protoc pinning recorded and doctor-checked; 100 seeds × 3 fresh processes byte-identical; go/no-go recorded in the decision log (§16).

## Out of scope
The Consensus port and Ready loop (W13). Never patch vote logic; never write our own Raft.

## Notes for the future
- FAILURE HANDLING IS SPECIAL: if the spike fails, the bead is NOT closed (closing a blocker would unblock dependants). `./dev commit --close W02 --failed` records the evidence report, labels the bead `failed`+`needs-owner`, and leaves it OPEN so dependants stay blocked until the owner's recorded plan revision (D-70).
- Fallback (recorded, not improvised): OpenRaft 0.9.x behind the same Consensus port with fully controlled runtime and entropy; switching is a plan revision in §16, never a quiet change (§7.3). If OpenRaft is adopted, R-03 (madsim/turmoil rejection) is reopened.
- raft-rs 0.7 hardwires the election-timeout range shape to [election_tick, 2×election_tick); the entropy-only patch does not change that — config validation (W08) encodes it.

PLAN.md wins over this bead on any disagreement (§0.4). Plan refs: §7.3, §12.2 W02, D-05, D-57, RISK-1, §11.4 (failed spikes).

comments.author: SunnyDog
comments.text:
SunnyDog — W03.2 contract readings where PLAN.md §8.4 is silent (owner confirmation wanted; cheap to change before W04/W10/W30/W31 consume the spec):
1. `not_leader.details.leader_hint` = the believed leader's node ID (NodeId). `Location` already carries its URL.
2. `limit` names the configuration parameter that refused: capacity_exceeded ∈ {max_live_keys, max_live_bytes} (DM-6); history_full ∈ {max_log_entries, max_history_bytes} (DM-7).
3. `nodes` = every configured voter's client URL (http://host:port), in ascending node-ID order, 1–5 entries (§8.6 example).
4. `details` is always present (possibly {}), and every error schema is closed. Read-side `invalid_request`/`busy` carry no write fields at all. `unavailable` can answer reads (node shutting down) with `nodes` only.
5. 405/415 (§8.4 "may") use the envelope with code `invalid_request`; no new code is added, and they are not declared per operation.
6. Per-operation error sets: GET/SCAN/status = 400, 404 (GET only), 429, 503 (unavailable|recovering); PUT/CAS = 307, 400, 409, 413, 429, 503, 504, 507 (capacity_exceeded|history_full); DELETE = the same minus 413, and 507 is history_full only (DM-6 never refuses a DELETE); health/ready = 503 recovering. health/live and /v1/cluster declare no errors (§8 silent on /v1/cluster during recovery).
7. TerminalResult (status lookup) now also admits the version_mismatch and capacity_exceeded envelopes; request_id_conflict and history_full are never stored results.
8. New byte-limit extensions beside x-maxUtf8Bytes: x-maxBodyBytes: 524288 on the PUT and CAS request bodies, and x-maxPageUtf8Bytes: 1048576 on ScanPage (machine-readable for W08's limits-registry cross-check, §7.10).

title: W03: Complete api/openapi.yaml per the API contract, with fixtures
description:
## Context
OpenAPI-first (D-12): `api/openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1.0) is the precise HTTP contract, completed BEFORE any server code is written. The independent conformance suite (W31) derives from it; on conflict with PLAN.md §8, the plan wins (§0.4). This item authors the complete spec and its test fixtures.

## Requirements covered
F-1…F-10 (all operations incl. request IDs, routing, status), O-1 (health + cluster endpoints).

## Area
`api` (api/openapi.yaml + fixtures).

## Depends on
W01 (workspace + `./dev check` plumbing for the SPEC check).

## Design & key rules (the contract, condensed from §8)
- Base path `/v1`; strict JSON (unknown fields, duplicate members, bad UTF-8/numbers → 400 invalid_request); keys are QUERY parameters, never path segments (keys may contain `/ ? &`); RFC 3986 percent-decoding with an unescaped `+` REJECTED (form-encoding ambiguity would corrupt keys; literal plus = %2B, space = %20); every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`; byte limits recorded via `x-maxUtf8Bytes` (JSON Schema length counts characters, not bytes); writes require `Idempotency-Key`: 32 lowercase hex chars (128 bits); integers are JSON numbers validated < 2^53.
- Endpoints: PUT /v1/kv?key=K {value} → {request_id,index,version,replayed,served_by}; GET /v1/kv?key=K → {key,value,version,served_by{node_id,applied_index}}; DELETE /v1/kv?key=K → {…existed…}; POST /v1/cas?key=K {expected:{kind:absent|version},value}; GET /v1/scan?start&end&after&limit → {items,has_more,next_after,served_by}; GET /v1/requests/{id} → state known (embedded original result) | unknown; GET /v1/health/live (lifecycle starting|recovering|ready|failed); GET /v1/health/ready (200 only when a complete committed read view is available); GET /v1/cluster (role, term, leader, indices, peers).
- Error envelope: {"error":{code,message,details}} with exactly three write-details shapes: (1) terminal execution results (version_mismatch, capacity_exceeded): request_id, index, replayed, decision — immutable; (2) conflict refusal (request_id_conflict): request_id, original_index; (3) non-terminal refusals (307 not_leader, 429 busy, 503 unavailable/recovering, 504 unknown_outcome, 507 history_full): request_id + attempt_state (not_submitted|submitted) + code-specific fields. 400/413 carry request_id only when a well-formed Idempotency-Key was present.
- Outcome table (§8.4): 307 not_leader (Location = leader, same path+query); 409 version_mismatch (TERMINAL, consumes the ID); 409 request_id_conflict; 413 too_large; 429 busy; 503 unavailable (+nodes)/recovering (+lifecycle); 504 unknown_outcome (+guidance retry_same_request_or_query_status, +nodes); 507 capacity_exceeded (TERMINAL committed decision) vs 507 history_full (not submitted, retry only after v2 compaction) — two distinct codes by design (D-54, to avoid RISK-15 double-writes).
- Per-operation response schemas: a PUT cannot validate as a DELETE result.

## Acceptance
- Validates as OpenAPI 3.1; every endpoint, status, code, byte limit (x-maxUtf8Bytes) and example of §8 present; per-operation response schemas; positive and negative fixtures pass `./dev check SPEC`; NO server code.

## Out of scope
Any server implementation; the peer channel (`POST /raft` on peer addresses) is internal and excluded from the public contract.

## Notes for the future
- Client guidance strings live in the spec descriptions (307 → follow with same ID; 504 → retry same ID or query status; an error on a later attempt is never evidence an earlier attempt did not commit).
- SCAN semantics: range [start,end) byte-wise UTF-8 order; `after` exclusive continuation; item cap 1–128 (default 32) and 1 MiB decoded-bytes page cap; has_more/next_after; no server-side cursor.
- A late contract change joins the critical path — get this right early (§12.4).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §8 (all), D-09, D-12, D-29, D-35, D-54, R-11, R-22, R-23.

SunnyDog — design notes and readings for W04.1:
- D-77 by type: NodeId (1..=2^53-1), Term and LogIndex (0..=2^53-1) and Version (1..=2^53-1) refuse anything else at construction, through one OutOfRange{quantity, value} error, so every value the core reports is a safe JSON integer. checked_next and checked_prev return None at the edges.

comments.text:
SunnyDog — W04.3 design (crates/types, std only), drafted on W04.2's tree as cc_1 asked:
- Inbound port: trait Inbound { fn step(&mut self, Input) -> Vec<Effect> }. Input = Client{attempt, op} | Peer{from, bytes} | Tick | SyncDone{seq, incarnation}. Effect = Send | Append | Truncate | Sync{seq, incarnation} | Respond | Log | Observe. Effect order is documented as binding. Sync carries the requesting incarnation so the adapter echoes it, and Input::is_stale_completion(current) recognises old completions (§7.2, B-17).
- Client port types: AttemptId; ClientOp = Write | Get | Scan | Status. ScanRange refuses start > end (§8.5). Response = Written{result, replayed, served_by} | Conflict | Found | NotFound | Page | Status | Refused(Refusal). ScanPage.continuation is an Option<Key>, so has_more/next_after cannot disagree (CD-2). A test proves the core can produce every §8.4 code except the boundary's invalid_request and too_large.
- In-process ports: Entropy::next_u64(EntropyStream); JournalRead::read_at(ByteCount, ReadLen <= 256 KiB); DataDir {lock, create_journal, sync_dir}; core-owned StorageError (no std::io types).
- READING 1 (scope): the Consensus port is defined here (W13.1 says "implement the Consensus port defined in W04"): propose/step/tick/ready/advance/applied/status over core types (Entry, HardState, Ready, LightReady, OutboundMessage bytes, Status with Progress, Role). No raft-rs type crosses it; W13 may refine against the pinned 0.7.0 API under its own reservation.
- READING 2 (scope): the telemetry events are minimal (LogEvent: RoleChanged, LifecycleChanged, Dropped; Observation: Applied, Responded). The observation schema itself is a W10/W36 document (T-12); W14 and W36 add variants.

title: W04: Domain types, newtypes, enums, error type and all ports
description:
## Context
Ports first (§11.7): the domain types and port definitions are created early so the production, simulation and oracle tracks can all proceed in parallel against stable interfaces. This crate is the heart of the hexagonal architecture (CD-1): the deterministic core defines ports in its OWN types; adapters translate; dependencies point inward only.

## Requirements covered
CD-1 (hexagonal), CD-2 (invalid states unrepresentable), CD-3 (parse, don't validate), CD-4 (distinct types per quantity), CD-5 (exhaustive matching), CD-11 (boring over clever; doc comments stating invariants), DM-1 (key: UTF-8, 1–256 bytes after decoding, stored exactly, no normalisation), DM-2 (value: UTF-8, 0–65,536 bytes after decoding), DM-4 (byte-wise lexicographic key order), T-1 (deterministic logic reaches time/randomness/network/disk only through ports).

## Area
`types` (crates/types).

## Depends on
W01 (workspace, lints), W03 (the error enum must match the spec's codes exactly — registry condition 5 later checks this).

## Design & key rules
- Newtypes (CD-4): NodeId, ClusterId, Term, LogIndex, Version, Tick, RequestId, ByteCount, PageSize — no bare integers cross a module boundary; comparing Version with LogIndex needs an explicit conversion; arithmetic is checked.
- Smart constructors (CD-3): `Key::parse` enforces DM-1 (255/256/257-byte cases, multibyte, composed vs decomposed Unicode are DIFFERENT keys); `Value::parse` enforces DM-2 (empty OK, 64 KiB max). Private fields; the core never re-checks.
- Enums (CD-2): node lifecycle Starting → Recovering → Ready → Failed; attempt NotSubmitted | Submitted | Terminal(result) — never independent booleans (unknown outcome is a RESPONSE about a Submitted attempt, not a fourth state); ExpectedVersion Absent | Version(v); Mutation (Put/Delete/Cas); error enum matching every spec code.
- Ports (§7.2): inbound `step(input) → effects`; effect ports returned as VALUES (Send, Append/Sync, Respond, Log/Observe) executed by the composition root, completions come back as inputs (SyncDone carries the node incarnation — completions from a previous incarnation are ignored); in-process ports called synchronously (entropy; bounded byte-storage reads, because raft-rs storage callbacks are synchronous). Effects are emitted in deterministic order. Port types are owned by the core.
- Every public domain type documents its invariants (CD-11 lint).

## Acceptance
- Key::parse/Value::parse enforce byte limits (255/256/257, multibyte, empty); all newtypes, ExpectedVersion, Mutation, RequestId, lifecycle and attempt enums, error enum matching spec codes, and all ports exist; compile-fail fixtures prove invalid states cannot be built; determinism lint rejects `Instant::now`; dependency-rule check fails when a deterministic crate depends on an adapter crate; W04's checks registered in registry/checks.toml with markers and selectors (shared-surface reservation) so DM-1/DM-2/T-1 have implemented coverage when they activate.

## Out of scope
State machine logic (W09), config (W08), any I/O.

## Notes for the future
- The registry rows requirement exists because requirement activation (W05/§10.13) demands an implemented covering check the moment the last listing bead closes — register as you build, never retrofit.
- No Raft-library type may ever cross the Consensus port (CD-1, replacement boundary §7.3).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §7.2, §5.2, §12.2 W04, D-19, D-20.

title: W05: Verification registry, T0 registry gate, traceability report
description:
## Context
Evidence over claims (P5) is enforced mechanically: a small machine-readable registry in `registry/` indexes ALL verification, and a T0 gate keeps plan ↔ registry ↔ code ↔ spec ↔ tests ↔ work graph consistent on every commit. This is the project's substitute for anyone "keeping track" by memory, and the guard against vacuous coverage (D-22, RISK-13).

## Requirements covered
P5; the whole of §10.13.

## Area
`registry` (registry/*.toml), `xtask` (the gate + report code).

## Depends on
W01 (xtask/gate), W03 (spec for conditions 5–6), W04 (code markers to validate), W06 (workgraph.toml for condition 8).

## Design & key rules
- Files: `registry/requirements.toml` (one row per §6 requirement: id, level MUST/SHOULD/MAY, status planned|active, title, disposition notes); `registry/checks.toml` (one row per check: id, kind, covers (req IDs), api (operation IDs/error codes), class (§10.15 claim class), tier, run (exact `./dev check` selector), min_cases (non-zero), catches (bug variants only)); `registry/workgraph.toml` (from W06).
- Code linking: every check declares its id in code as a greppable marker (e.g. `// check: K-5`) AND its row names an executable selector; marker alone is not enough — the selector must run ≥ min_cases assertions.
- The gate FAILS on: (1) requirements.toml differs from §6 (plan wins); (2) an ACTIVE MUST requirement with no implemented covering check; (3) implemented check without exactly one code marker, or marker without row; (4) implemented selector that does not resolve — in T0 the selector check is STATIC (resolve + list cases); min_cases execution is enforced by the tier that runs the check (D-72, so T0 never executes T1–T3 campaigns); (5) spec error codes differ from the domain error enum, or an operation lacks a handler; (6) an operation/error code no conformance test exercises; (7) a bug-variant row without a designated catcher; (8) workgraph.toml differs from §12.2, has a cycle, or disagrees with imported bead dependencies (plan:W edges only).
- Conditions 5–6 are REPORTED, not failed, until W32 closes (W18 implements only PUT/GET; enforcing earlier would fail every commit between W18 and W32 — D-49).
- Status lifecycle: requirements start planned; a requirement becomes ACTIVE when ALL work items listing it in their Reqs have closed (activation derived from workgraph.toml by `./dev commit --close`, never typed by hand — the gate REJECTS hand-edited statuses, rule 12). Check statuses are declared, forward-only, protected like oracle manifests (D-56): a broken selector can never silently demote a check to planned. "Passed on a build" is computed from receipts, never stored.
- W05 initialises requirements.toml with correct statuses for beads already closed by then.
- T1 renders `reports/traceability.md`: each requirement, status, qualifications, covering checks with claim classes and latest receipts.

## Acceptance
- Each of the eight gate conditions demonstrated by a fixture that makes it fail (5–6 in report mode; condition 8 against W06's workgraph.toml); a hand-edited requirement status is rejected; requirements.toml matches §6; the traceability report renders.

## Out of scope
The bead importer (W06); gate TIERS and scheduling (W46); bug-variant execution (W45).

## Notes for the future
- B-21 (meta bug variant, W45) will mutate a registry row in a sandboxed tree copy and expect THIS gate to catch it — keep the gate honest.
- The registry gate catches mechanical drift continuously; semantic drift is the drift audits' job (§11.9).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.13, D-22, D-56, D-72, RISK-13.

title: W06: Work-graph manifest (workgraph.toml) and idempotent bead import
description:
## Context
The work graph lives in three places that must never drift: PLAN.md §12.2 (authoritative), `registry/workgraph.toml` (machine mirror), and the beads tracker (execution state). W06 builds the mirror and the idempotent importer. Plan changes flow plan → workgraph.toml → beads, NEVER the other way (§11.11).

## Requirements covered
G1 (the dev-process goal itself), §11.11.

## Area
`registry`, `xtask`.

## Depends on
W01.

## Design & key rules
- `workgraph.toml`: one row per §12.2 item — id, title, deps, reqs, area, milestone (derived from m0–m5 epic labels), accept (executable acceptance selectors; the §12.2 acceptance column is their prose description), and the tracker's bead ID once imported (recorded, never guessed).
- `./dev beads import --dry-run` prints the diff; `./dev beads import` applies idempotently: beads are identified by their `plan:W<nn>` label; repeated imports never duplicate; hand-created beads (this very bead set!) are ADOPTED by label.
- The importer uses supported `br` CLI operations only — it never hand-edits the tracker's files; `br` never runs git itself (§11.1).
- The drift check (feeding registry condition 8): workgraph.toml vs §12.2 on id/deps/reqs/area (ranges like "F-1…F-10" expand); the bead comparison covers ONLY edges between plan:W beads — bug and discovered-work beads (and the sub:W subtask beads) may add edges freely.
- Cycles are rejected.

## Acceptance
- workgraph.toml matches §12.2 and the drift check fails on a changed dependency; --dry-run prints the diff; a second import creates no duplicates; plan-ID ↔ bead-ID mapping stored; cycles rejected.

## Out of scope
The eight-condition registry gate itself (W05); milestone epic management.

## Notes for the future
- After import, run `bv --robot-insights` (no cycles) and `bv --robot-suggest` (missing deps, duplicates); fix findings in the PLAN first (§0.4), then re-import (§11.2 step 4).
- The current bead set was hand-created with exact §12.3 edges and plan:W labels precisely so this importer adopts it unchanged — a mismatch found during adoption is a defect in either this bead set or workgraph.toml; reconcile against PLAN.md §12.2.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §11.11, §10.13 cond. 8, §11.2 step 3.
