title: W43: Full-operation workload profiles + capacity heals + journal exhaustion
description:
## Context
Full-operation workload profiles: the simulator finally exercises DELETE, CAS, SCAN, status, misuse and the CAPACITY regimes — including the subtle capacity-profile heal adaptations that make convergence judgeable when the normal catch-up marker cannot be written.

## Requirements covered
§10.3 (profiles), §10.2 (capacity heals), DM-7 (journal-exhaustion failure mode).

## Area
`sim` (workload + nemesis profile wiring).

## Depends on
W27, W28, W29 (the operations), W36 (generator), W37 (heal), W41 (coverage cells).

## Design & key rules
- Profiles: CAS-heavy contention; delayed retries long after the original; all-node restart; asymmetric links; long pauses; read isolation (reads on a minority node); boundary-sized values; misuse; capacity (deliberately hitting DM-6 and DM-7 with SMALL TEST LIMITS — the config margin formula applies to small limits too, so capacity profiles are not flaky).
- Capacity heal adaptations (D-53, D-64): DM-6 (live-quota) profiles PRE-CREATE the marker key during Baseline and overwrite it with an equal-size value, so the quota can never refuse the marker. DM-7 (history) profiles write NO marker: first ALL client activity stops (recorded in the trace); then over a quiet period (default 100 ticks) the god view must show a stable current-term leader and, on every recoverable node, last log index = commit index = applied index with identical digests (CERTIFIED DRAIN — no uncommitted entry anywhere can commit later); only then are outstanding writes resolved by a STATUS LOOKUP ON EVERY RECOVERABLE NODE: a stored terminal result resolves with its index; unknown on ALL recoverable nodes now genuinely proves the write never executed and never can (history never expires + full prefix applied + no pending suffix) ⇒ resolved `not executed`. A write refused history_full with no submitted attempt resolves `refused`; one with ANY submitted attempt resolves only by the lookup rule — a later refusal never resolves an earlier submitted attempt.
- Journal exhaustion scenario (D-61): drive one node to its local journal-byte hard stop ⇒ it stops appending, moves to `failed` (visible in health), drops peer traffic (counted), answers clients `recovering`; reads elsewhere continue. An explicitly accepted v1 failure mode — tested, not hidden.
- Completes the operation/outcome cells of registry/coverage.toml: every operation and outcome cell of the coverage matrix is reachable.

## Acceptance
- DELETE, CAS, SCAN, status, misuse and capacity profiles run; the capacity-profile heal follows §10.2 (DM-6 pre-created marker; DM-7 certified drain + status-lookup resolution); a journal-exhaustion scenario drives a node to its hard stop → failed while reads elsewhere continue; every operation and outcome cell of the coverage matrix is reachable.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.3, §10.2 (heal), DM-7, D-53, D-61, D-64.

title: W45: Bug variants B-01..B-22 and the checker self-test
description:
## Context
The checker self-test: deliberately broken build variants that the checkers MUST catch. This is the mechanical guard for P9 (oracles are sacred) and RISK-3 (agents weakening checkers to get green): a checker weakened to pass will fail its self-test. A variant counts as CAUGHT only if its targeted scenario reached the injected behaviour (trigger counter proves it), the unmutated control build passes the same scenario, and the designated catcher reports the specified failure class. A variant that merely crashes in its constructor proves nothing.

## Requirements covered
T-6 (test-builds only), P9, §10.6.

## Area
Touches many: `node`, `statemachine`, `raft_adapter`, `journal`, `server`, `model`, `conformance`, `sim`, `checker`, `registry`, `xtask` — reserve per leaf module as you go.

## Depends on
W05 (registry/B-21), W31 (conformance/B-20), W32 (real server for B-20), W41 (verdicts), W43 (profiles that reach the behaviours).

## Design & key rules
- CODE variants B-01…B-20 behind ONE `bug-variants` feature; each site a registered `bug_switch!(B-xx)` invocation; the static parity check (§10.18) allowlists exactly these sites; a release-build check proves the feature off and the sites compiled to nothing. The sanctioned T-2 exception (D-47).
- The variant table (id → behaviour → designated catcher): B-01 ack at proposal → K-1/K-10; B-02 vote released before term/vote sync, crash, revote → K-11 (K-8 under crash); B-03 append ack before durable → K-11/K-1; B-04 sync no-op → K-1 under crashes; B-05 publish uncommitted reads → K-5; B-06 stale/future served_by.applied_index → K-5; B-07 SCAN page from two prefixes → K-5; B-08 CAS at admission → K-4/K-10; B-09 CAS ignores expectation → K-4; B-10 dedup off → K-2; B-11 expiring ID window → K-2 (delayed-retry profile); B-12 replay returns duplicate index → K-2/K-4; B-13 stored result for different-command reuse → K-2/conformance; B-14 version reset on delete/re-create → K-4; B-15 submitted timeout reported failed/not_submitted → K-12; B-16 double vote in a term (persisted vote dropped across restart — injected in raft_adapter, NEVER in vendor, D-57) → K-8; B-17 stale-incarnation sync completion accepted → K-11/K-1; B-18 skip catch-up after heal → K-9/K-7; B-19 one election timeout from ambient randomness (wired at the TEST COMPOSITION ROOT into one node's adapter — no deterministic crate gains a dependency, D-74) → K-14 with a reliable changing-counter fixture; B-20 well-formed response with wrong status/decision → conformance suite.
- META variants: B-21 (remove a MUST requirement's only check / make a filter select zero tests) → registry gate; B-22 (weaken the reference model re duplicates or real-time order) → checker unit fixtures + the fixed negative-history corpus. Applied as scripted mutations to a SANDBOXED COPY of the tree, never the working tree; caught = the designated gate/fixture suite fails on the mutated copy with the expected failure class while the unmutated control passes.
- If several checkers fire, all are reported; the designated one must be among them.
- Oracle protection: requirement manifests, regression seeds, bug-variant expectations, lint policy and the negative-history corpus are protected — removal, skipping or silent reclassification fails the gate; receipts include their hashes; a changed checker cannot supply its own acceptance evidence in the same unchecked step.

## Acceptance
- For every variant B-01…B-22: trigger reached (counter), control passes, designated catcher fires with the specified failure class (B-16 in raft_adapter, B-19 at the test composition root, B-20 against the real server, B-21 against the registry gate, B-22 against model fixtures); oracle-protection fixtures reject weakening.

## Out of scope
New checkers (they exist); gate-tier wiring of the self-test cadence (W46: T1/T3 run it).

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.6, D-47, D-57, D-74, RISK-3.

title: W46: Gate tiers, receipts, local scheduler, failure outbox, prune
description:
## Context
The staged gate tiers and the local scheduler — the heartbeat of the whole process. T0 on every commit (≤ 2 min target), T1 hourly, T2 nightly, T3 at release; all local, all receipted, all honest about staging (`implemented` checks enforced, `planned` checks reported). Scheduled failures become tracked work AUTOMATICALLY through a durable outbox — no agent needs to notice a red gate (D-39).

## Requirements covered
P7, P10, §10.10, §10.11.

## Area
`xtask`.

## Depends on
W05 (registry staging), W07 (candidate/accept isolation), W31 (conformance in T1), W42 (campaigns).

## Design & key rules
- Tier contents (§10.10): T0 = format, lints, dependency-rule + ledger checks, registry gate + work-graph drift, unit/property/compile-fail for changed crates AND their reverse dependencies (incl. differential tests, goldens, schema tests), UBS on staged files, ~50 small sim seeds, 2 replay pairs, the corpus or its fast subset (the full corpus while it fits the T0 budget, then a fixed reviewed fast subset — §10.9), negative-history fixtures. T1 (hourly, low CPU priority, ≤ 15 min target) = T0 on the whole workspace + full corpus + ~2,000 swarm seeds + 16 replay pairs + checker self-test + conformance vs model server, real single node AND a fresh per-run 5-node cluster (ephemeral ports/dirs under .local/gates/<run-id>/, NEVER the owner's config/local.toml cluster) + crash probes and lifecycle smoke + doctor on every node dir afterwards + parity + fuzz-corpus replay + coverage report with ratchet + traceability. T2 (nightly, resumable, one at a time) = full corpus + ~10,000 fresh seeds + 64 replay pairs + all dedicated profiles + time-boxed fuzz + campaign coverage + matrix/measurements reports. T3 (manual, release) = everything + ≥ 100k seeds + 100 replay pairs + every bug variant + clean-state rehearsal + required coverage cells + audits complete.
- Staging: each tier runs the listed checks whose registry status is implemented+; planned checks reported with their implementing work item, never failing the tier, never filing beads. T3 accepts NO planned check anywhere.
- Pass criteria (§10.11): T0 — every selected check executed ≥ its registered min_cases and passed; duration recorded; sustained overrun files a bead rather than failing commits. T1 — 0 checker violations, 0 incomplete runs, every implemented variant caught, conformance 100% for implemented tests, probes+smoke pass, determinism clean. T2 — T1's sim criteria over the campaign; campaign finished; reports produced. T3 — 0 violations across ≥ 100k seeds on the release build; every required coverage cell non-zero; every MUST passed; no open P0, no open P1 BUG beads (W51/W52 exempt while they run).
- Tree isolation: T1/T2/T3 each materialise their own per-run tree directory under the same git-isolation discipline as the candidate (D-74). A stopped/sleeping machine has MISSED runs, not passed ones; an interrupted campaign stays incomplete with completed/remaining seeds explicit.
- Failure path: write an immutable failure receipt + durable local OUTBOX item; keep the crash pack; fingerprint the failure (checker, class, signature); create or update EXACTLY ONE br bug with seed, replay command, crash-pack path, build, affected requirements. Tracker unavailable ⇒ the outbox item stays pending, visible in ./dev status; a failure is never dropped.
- `./dev prune`: the ONLY sanctioned deleter of generated .local/ artifacts — keep last 5 gate runs, last 5 accept trees, every failing run's artifacts (Q9); logs every removal in a receipt.
- `./dev schedule install|status`: local timers for T1 hourly / T2 nightly; resource arbitration (§11.12): one campaign at a time, T0 > T1 > T2 priority.

## Acceptance
- Each tier selects its specified contents among implemented+ checks and reports planned ones; zero-test and incomplete runs fail; a planned check never files a bead; a forced scheduled failure plus a tracker outage yields EXACTLY ONE bead once the tracker returns; ./dev prune applies the retention rule and logs removals in a receipt; receipts carry tree IDs.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.10, §10.11, §11.12, D-15, D-39, D-49, D-58, D-74, Q9.

Tiers select implemented+ checks and report planned; zero-test and incomplete runs fail; planned never files a bead; forced failure + tracker outage yields exactly one bead after recovery; prune applies retention with receipts; receipts carry tree IDs
- [ ] Every gate run tees per-check logs into the receipt directory; a failing check's receipt entry includes the exact re-run command

title: W47: Measurements-under-failure report
description:
## Context
Measurements under failure — REPORTED, never gated, in v1 (Measurement claim class; a latency gate would invite gaming, R-09). Simulation metrics use virtual time; real-probe metrics use real monotonic time, labelled separately. Raw samples plus min/median/p95/max; never fabricated numbers.

## Requirements covered
§10.12.

## Area
`sim`, `xtask`.

## Depends on
W24 (real-probe metrics), W42 (campaign machinery).

## Design & key rules — the metric table
- Election time: leader crash/isolation (and separately the first election trigger) → first new leader committing a current-term entry; detection-inclusive and election-only durations.
- Write unavailability window: last successful probe write before the fault → first after; window, probe interval, censored cases.
- Convergence time: all faults healed → all recoverable nodes applied the marker with identical digests; by fault profile and survivor set.
- Restart catch-up: restart begins (recording when recovery reached Ready) → node applies the chosen marker; local recovery vs replication catch-up separately.
- Unknown-outcome rate: write attempts AND distinct logical writes as denominators; unknown responses and disconnects before resolution; final resolutions; unresolved count.
- Recovery time vs history size: process start → lifecycle Ready, per history-size profile (RISK-4 evidence).
- T2 produces reports/measurements-<date>.md. K-9 still enforces its functional bound under the envelope — distinct from any latency gate.

## Acceptance
- Every §10.12 metric with raw samples, definitions, virtual/real labels and censored counts.

title: W48: Parity check — static branch rejection + dynamic semantic agreement + probe twins
description:
## Context
The parity check: proof that production and simulation run the SAME semantic code (P3) — the property that makes simulation evidence meaningful for production at all (RISK-7).

## Requirements covered
P3, T-2, §10.18.

## Area
`xtask`, `sim`.

## Depends on
W17 (sim root), W24 (probes to twin), W32 (real cluster).

## Design & key rules
- STATIC: a T0 check rejects cfg-gated or environment-specific branches in deterministic crates — except the registered bug_switch! sites (allowlisted, verified absent from release builds) — and verifies both composition roots use the same state machine, controller, Raft adapter, journal engine and command codec (dependency-graph comparison).
- DYNAMIC: a scripted sequential scenario (writes, CAS, deletes, scans, a restart) runs in the simulator, against a real single node and against a real cluster; runs must agree on SEMANTIC TRANSITIONS — the sequence of first executions per key (commands, decisions, value states), with versions compared through each run's own execution order (versions are log indices, so absolute values legitimately differ across topologies with different election/no-op histories). Exact index equality asserted only between runs constructed to share an identical Raft entry sequence (the simulator's scripted single-voter twin of the real single node).
- PROBE TWINS: each §10.17 crash probe has a scripted simulator twin; their observable outcomes must match (D-71 assigns twin ownership here).

## Acceptance
- The static check rejects a planted cfg-gated semantic branch; the scripted scenario gives identical semantic results in simulation, a real node and a real cluster; each probe's scripted twin runs and outcomes match.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.18, P3, T-2, R-24, RISK-7.
acceptance_criteria:
Static check rejects a planted cfg-gated semantic branch; scripted scenario agrees across sim, real node and cluster; every probe twin matches

- Final audit: fresh-context, filed before the campaign starts; findings above P2 must be closed first.

title: W53: Parser-boundary fuzz targets and code-coverage reporting
description:
## Context
Owner additions v1.3 (D-66, D-67): coverage-guided fuzzing exactly where the simulator is blind (arbitrary-byte parse boundaries — the simulator only generates well-formed traffic), and code-coverage reporting because requirement-level traceability cannot see untested branches and nobody reads the code.

## Requirements covered
§10.19, CD-3 (the fuzzed boundaries), CD-8 (no-panic enforced mechanically on decode paths).

## Area
`fuzz` (top-level cargo-fuzz package), `xtask`.

## Depends on
W09 (command codec), W11 (journal scanner), W18 (HTTP parsers), W21 (completes the peer-transport wiring this target exercises; the envelope decoder itself is W13 code, a transitive dependency — §12.2 lists W21), W46 (T1/T2 slots).

## Design & key rules
- Four targets: (1) journal recovery + resync scanner — never panics on arbitrary bytes; classifies every input clean/torn-tail/corruption; never erases synced frames within the crash model; (2) canonical command codec — never panics; decode(encode(x)) == x; rejects oversized; (3) HTTP JSON body + query parsers — never panic; strict-JSON and percent-decoding rules hold; (4) peer envelope decoder — never panics; mismatched identity always drops.
- `fuzz/` pins its OWN rust-toolchain.toml (a specific nightly — cargo-fuzz needs it); `./dev doctor` verifies it; fuzz builds NEVER count as the pinned "same build" for T-3 determinism claims.
- T2 runs each target time-boxed (default 10 min, rotating targets across nights); every finding minimized into the append-only `fuzz/corpus/` (and a golden vector where it is a journal case) and replayed DETERMINISTICALLY in T1; a fuzz run that executed zero inputs is incomplete (P10); "found nothing new" is never a pass criterion.
- Coverage: T1 runs cargo llvm-cov over its test run; `./dev report coverage-code` renders per-crate line/region coverage for deterministic-core crates; T2 adds CAMPAIGN-MODE coverage (llvm-cov over a sim campaign — a direct probe of simulator blind spots). Measurement class, NEVER a gate; the RATCHET: per-crate coverage of deterministic-core crates may not decrease vs the last T1 baseline — a decrease files a P2 bead; the baseline updates only by a closing bead's receipt. Uncovered regions listed in the traceability report for drift audits.

## Acceptance
- All four cargo-fuzz targets exist and prove no-panic (+ round-trip where applicable); a seeded finding is minimized into fuzz/corpus/ and replayed in T1; fuzz/ pins its nightly, doctor-verified; ./dev report coverage-code renders per-crate llvm-cov with the ratchet; the T2 fuzz slot and campaign-mode coverage report run.

PLAN.md wins over this bead (§0.4). Plan refs: §10.19, D-66, D-67.
